==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=WinForms&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests.Windows/Plugins/WinFormsTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=WinForms&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
// Verify.WinForms: Renders a WinForms form, control or context menu to png and verifies the image.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.WinForms
// Note: The only output is a png; there is no text snapshot, so an exact byte comparison is
// brittle. VerifierSettings.UseSsimForPng() or an image comparer plugin makes it tolerant.
// Note: Converters are registered for Form, ContextMenuStrip, UserControl and Control, each
// producing one png.
// Note: Showing a control installs a WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext on the thread, which would
// deadlock Verify's async IO, so the converter saves and restores it around the rendering.
// Note: Unlike Verify.Xaml, no STA apartment attribute is needed.
// Note: The sample form is nested in the test class: the generated class library is not a WinForms
// project, so a Form cannot live there.
// Note: WinForms and WPF define many of the same control names, so selecting Verify.Xaml as well
// makes Label, Button and their siblings ambiguous; the sample qualifies the one it uses.
// Note: Windows only: the test project targets net10.0-windows and sets UseWindowsForms.
public class WinFormsTests
{
    // The form is drawn to a bitmap and the png is the snapshot, so a change to the layout is
    // reviewed as a picture rather than inferred from control properties.
    [Fact]
    public Task FormUsage()
    {
        return Verify(new SampleForm());
    }

    // A menu has no surface of its own to draw on, so it gets a converter that hosts it first.
    // Verifying it covers the item text and ordering a user actually sees.
    [Fact]
    public Task ContextMenuStrip()
    {
        var menu = new ContextMenuStrip();
        var items = menu.Items;

        items.Add(new ToolStripMenuItem("About"));
        items.Add(new ToolStripMenuItem("Exit"));
        return Verify(menu);
    }

    // Rendering differs slightly between Windows versions and runtimes. A snapshot per runtime
    // keeps a shared machine and a build agent from fighting over the same file.
    [Fact]
    public Task UniqueForRuntime()
    {
        return Verify(new SampleForm())
            .UniqueForRuntime();
    }

    // Stands in for a form of your own. Nested here rather than in the class library, which
    // is not a WinForms project, so a Form cannot live there.
    class SampleForm :
        Form
    {
        public SampleForm()
        {
            Text = "Sample";
            ClientSize = new(300, 120);
            // Qualified because WPF defines a Label too, and selecting Verify.Xaml as well
            // puts both namespaces in the same project as global usings.
            Controls.Add(
                new System.Windows.Forms.Label
                {
                    Text = "Hello",
                    Location = new(10, 10),
                    AutoSize = true
                });
        }
    }
}
